references.text: Jesus quotes directly from Isaiah 56:7, where God says: "my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples." This is the source text for the first part of Jesus' statement about the temple as "a house of prayer" (οἶκος προσευχῆς).

The second part of Jesus' statement, "a den of robbers" (σπήλαιον λῃστῶν), is taken from Jeremiah 7:11, where God asks: "Has this house, which bears my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes?" Jeremiah spoke against those who misused the temple while living in sin.
The parallel account in Matthew 21:13 describes the same event where Jesus drives out the merchants from the temple and quotes Isaiah and Jeremiah with nearly identical wording.
The parallel account in Mark 11:17 recounts the same event. Mark also includes the addition "for all nations" from Isaiah 56:7, which Luke omits here.

In John 2:16, a similar temple cleansing early in Jesus' ministry is described, where Jesus says: "Do not make my Father's house a marketplace!" Both events express Jesus' zeal for the temple as God's house.

Psalm 69:10 speaks of zeal for God's house: "For zeal for your house has consumed me." This psalm was linked to Jesus' temple cleansing in John 2:17 and highlights Jesus' passion for the holiness of the temple.

Zechariah 14:21 prophesies a future time when there will no longer be any merchants in the Lord's house. Jesus' action in the temple can be seen as a fulfillment of this prophecy concerning the cleansing of the temple.
